explanation: Aquatic ecosystems contain plankton, which are important freshwater and marine communities divided into phytoplankton (photosynthetic algae) and zooplankton (microscopic animals that feed on phytoplankton). Freshwater bodies like lakes are divided into distinct life zones: 1) Littoral zone: the shallow zone closest to the shore. 2) Limnetic zone: the open, sunlit surface waters. 3) Profundal zone: the deep, dark zone below light penetration. 4) Benthic zone: the bottom soil-water interface.

questions.q: What is the difference between phytoplankton and zooplankton?
opts: Phytoplankton are microscopic animals, while zooplankton are photosynthetic algae.
Phytoplankton are photosynthetic algae, while zooplankton are tiny animals that feed on them.
Phytoplankton live in the profundal zone, while zooplankton live in the littoral zone.
Phytoplankton are found only in salt water, while zooplankton are only in fresh water.
